rationale: Self-hosted mail server operators — typically solo developers, small agencies, or SMB sysadmins who have already invested significant time in DMARC/DKIM/SPF setup — feel real pain when their carefully-configured server still bounces into spam due to shared-range blocklists like UCEPROTECT L3. Willingness to pay is plausible but indirect: the segment chose self-hosting specifically to avoid paying SendGrid/Mailgun, so price sensitivity is high and the buyer more likely pays only if the alternative is switching away from self-hosting entirely. Operational autonomy scores 6 because the core monitoring loop (check blocklists, alert, generate remediation guidance) is automatable, but meaningful remediation often requires operator-specific context (ISP, IP range, hosting provider) that needs human follow-through — delivery of genuine resolution rather than just reporting is hard to automate fully. Build gates for operational_autonomy (6, needs 7) and willingness_to_pay (5, needs 5 — just meets threshold) mean the total qualifies for validate but the autonomy gate caps it there.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an automated email deliverability monitor that tracks blocklist status, config health (DMARC/DKIM/SPF/rDNS), and generates a plain-English remediation report for self-hosted mail server operators. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt pipeline that accepts a domain/IP as input via a simple intake form, queries public blocklist APIs (MXToolbox, UCEPROTECT, Spamhaus) and DNS records, then produces a prioritized action report — wrapped in a Stripe payment link ($15-29 one-time or $9/mo for continuous monitoring). Outreach targets self-hosters on ServerFault, Hacker News 'Ask HN', r/selfhosted, and Postfix/Dovecot forums with a free instant scan offer to generate leads; all outreach batches go out only after Youval approves them. Ongoing delivery is automated: users submit their domain, Claude runs checks and generates the report, Stripe handles billing, and email delivers the PDF — the only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any edge-case support replies flagged by Claude. The key risk to validate first: will this audience pay even $9/mo, or do they expect free tools like MXToolbox? Run a landing page with a paid CTA before building the full pipeline.
notes: operational_autonomy scored 6 (gate requires 7) — meaningful remediation guidance can be generated autonomously, but actual delisting from UCEPROTECT L3 (which charges $299 for 'express' removal or requires ISP-level action) is outside the tool's control, limiting the autonomy of delivering genuine resolution vs. just reporting. Validate whether users pay for diagnosis-only or expect the service to fix it.
